title: An Integrated Micro-Device System for Coral Growth and Monitoring
protocol: Inspect each module individually before assembly.
Test the tightness of each module using deionized water.
Connect all modules and pumps to form a circular water flow system.
Run the water through the system for at least 30 minutes.
Check all seams for leakage issues.
Apply bonding glue from the outside if any leaking occurs in bonding seams.
Tighten connections again if any leaking occurs in connection seams.
Replace sealing gasket if necessary due to leaks.
Evacuate and dry the water inside the modules after tightness testing.
Load appropriate contents into each module, such as bacterial culture substrate into microbial purification module.
Fix the loaded modules onto the baseboard using screws.
Connect inner circulation modules with outer circulation ones without coral culture module.
Test the assembled system for proper functioning.
Inject seawater through the water inlet of the seawater store module.
Continue injecting until the inner circulation modules are full and there is a 3 cm air gap in the seawater store module.
Turn on all switches and set both seawater pump voltages to 9 V.
Set the water temperature to 25 °C.
Set the cycle timer to "1 minute on and 1 minute off".
Set all three channels of the three-channel timer to "9:00 am on" and "5:00 pm off".
Monitor the system for at least 24 hours for any malfunction.
Clear bubbles in all modules except the seawater store module by lifting and shaking the system.
Add a diluted probiotic solution as the microbial source for the nitrification system.
Add 1 mL of the commercial microbiome source solution into 500 mL of seawater with stirring.
Inject 50 mL of the diluted microbiome solution and 10 µL of the commercial coral nutrition solution into the circulation system.
Switch on the inner circulation pump and air pump to culture the microbiome for 21 days.
Cut raw coral branches with length scales of 3-5 cm.
Adhere cut coral branches onto 3D-printed coral support bases.
Place adhered coral samples back into the original seawater tank for at least 7 days for recovery.
Fix the coral support base onto a rotation unit with glue.
Assemble the coral culture module and connect it to the outer circulation loop.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl to reconstitute human recombinant leptin.
Place the camera on top of the mini-photo studio for imaging.
Position the coral culture module in the center and at the bottom of the photo studio.
Capture images of the coral by rotating the outside handle to obtain full-angle views.
Inspect the baseboard daily for water stains or droplets to check for leaks.
Visually inspect the system's transparent cover shell for any signs of water leakage.
Perform a malfunction inspection regularly as part of routine maintenance.
Inspect the water temperature every day.
Check the pumps daily.
Verify light voltages on a daily basis.
Monitor air pump status each day.
Record timer status daily.
Visually check and record set water temperature.
Note real-time temperature during inspection.
Document transformer output voltages regularly.
Log UV lamp settings consistently.
Ensure timer is functioning properly.
Extract 10 mL of seawater using a syringe.
Dissolve additives in the extracted seawater.
Inject the solution back into the system.
Switch off power for the whole system.
Unplug the power cable for safety.
Remove coral culture module carefully.
Connect outside wastewater pipeline to outlet.
Rotate the system front-side down.
Switch on the outlet.
Let the inside seawater flow out of the system.
Discharge an appropriate amount of seawater.
Switch off the outlet.
Reset the system.
Inject newly prepared seawater into the system through the water inlet.
Install the coral culture module back into the system.
Switch on the system power.
Wait until the whole system goes back to normal.
Switch off the inner circulation pump for module replacement.
Loosen the fixing screws for the module to be replaced.
Disconnect the pipelines between joined modules.
Disassemble the module to be replaced from the system.
Assemble the new module into the system by connecting the pipelines.
Retighten the fixing screws.
Switch off the system power, and unplug the power cable.
Evacuate the seawater inside the system.
Disassemble the coral culture module from the system.
Disassemble the activated charcoal purification module from the system.
Disassemble the seawater store module from the system.
Disassemble the algae purification module from the system.
Disassemble the microbial purification module from the system.
Disassemble the UV lamp from the system.
Disassemble the circulation pumps from the system.
Disassemble the temperature control module from the system.
Clean all modules with pure water and surface active agents.
Sterilize the modules with 3% hydrogen peroxide solution.
Dry the modules at 40 °C for 12 h to ensure all water is evaporated.
Clean all pipelines and valves using the same surface active agents.
Sterilize all the modules, pipelines, and valves using 3% hydrogen peroxide solution before assembling the system.
Sterilize the bacterial culture substrate via autoclaving.
Sterilize Chaetomorpha algae with 75% ethanol solution.
Dry sterilized Chaetomorpha algae using sterile paper.
Add an air sterilizing filter between the air pump and the seawater store module.
Add a water sterilizing filter between the inlet and the three-way valve.
Introduce ozone into the system to eliminate remaining microbiome.
Wash off remaining disinfectant agents with sterile seawater three times.
Inject sterile seawater into the system.
